requirement:
Pass the `next` UUID exactly as returned by the previous page. The UUID
identifies the prepared result and determines the shape of the returned object.

```text
get_next_page({uuid: UUID}) -> object
```
rationale:
structural: The only structural obligation is the tool's interface: `get_next_page({uuid: UUID}) -> object`. The UUID identifies a prepared result and that result determines the returned object's shape. The clause "Pass the `next` UUID exactly as returned" describes what callers do, so it is not a build obligation.

Both roots cover the interface:
- `crates/trust-but-verify/src/agent/tools.rs#impl[GraphSession<'_, '_, D>/Conversation]/fn[tools]` declares a `get_next_page` tool. Its parameters schema is an object that requires a `uuid` string with format `uuid`.
- `crates/trust-but-verify/src/agent/tools.rs#impl[SessionTools<'a, D>]/fn[dispatch]` routes `get_next_page` to `self.pages.get(args)`.

The helper `crates/trust-but-verify/src/agent/pages.rs#impl[Pages<N, L>]/fn[get]` is reached from `dispatch`, so it needs no marker of its own. It reads `args["uuid"]`, parses it as a UUID, and looks up the retained prepared delivery by that UUID. It returns that stored result as is, so the UUID determines the returned object. It returns an error for an unknown UUID.

Both roots already carry the `{impl}` reference. I found no gap.

behavioral: The subject has two behavioral obligations. First, `get_next_page` takes a single `{uuid}` argument, the `next` value exactly as the previous page returned it. Second, that UUID identifies the prepared result, so the returned object has the shape of the originating tool's result. Invalid-UUID handling belongs to `pages.behavior`, which this requirement does not cover.

The tests cover both obligations:
- **Tool signature.** `crates/trust-but-verify/src/agent/tests.rs#fn[default_tool_accepts_scalar_results_and_keeps_the_exact_prefix]` asserts that `get_next_page` is offered and that its parameters are exactly `{type:object, required:[uuid], properties:{uuid:{type:string, format:uuid}}}`.
- **Passing `next` back unchanged.** Every continuation test passes the returned `next` value straight into `get_next_page`:
  - `application_tools_preserve_graph_tools_in_the_same_conversation` uses the node-read page UUID.
  - `outline_continuations_keep_the_file_and_complete_ordered_items`, `listing_continuations_return_complete_paths_from_the_original_listing` and `search_obligations_follow_delivery_and_keep_the_original_snapshot` use the UUIDs from their own pages.
- **Shape determined by the UUID.** The same `get_next_page` call returns a different object shape depending on which result the UUID names:
  - Outline pages (`outline_continuations_keep_the_file_and_complete_ordered_items`) carry `node` and `items`. The test checks each item's `node`, `file`, `selector` and `kind`.
  - Listing pages (`listing_continuations_return_complete_paths_from_the_original_listing`) carry `files`. The test checks each entry's `node` and `data`.
  - Search pages (`search_obligations_follow_delivery_and_keep_the_original_snapshot`) carry `matches` and `search_id`, with no `instructions` on later pages.
  - Text read pages (the root-read loop in the outline test, and `application_tools_preserve_graph_tools_in_the_same_conversation`) carry `text`, `next` and, for mapped sources, `children`. The tests assert the concatenated text and the full children list.

Each continuation test asserts the returned fields rather than only running the call. The behavior-side obligations (replay, errors, dependency recording, ordering) belong to `pages.behavior` and `pages.inputs`, so they need no separate test here.

text: :::{req} pages.mcp
Pass the `next` UUID exactly as returned by the previous page. The UUID
identifies the prepared result and determines the shape of the returned object.
```text
get_next_page({uuid: UUID}) -> object
:::{req} pages.behavior
Each page has the same result fields as the originating tool. Text reads return
successive portions of text. Listings, outlines, and searches return successive
arrays of whole entries in their original order. Only a page with a successor
includes `next`.
Reusing a UUID returns the same page from the original snapshot, including the
same successor UUID if more remains. A malformed UUID, an unknown UUID, or a UUID
from another conversation returns a tool error under
{cite}`requirements.sdk.graph.agent-harness.tool_agent.isolation`.
:::{req} pages.inputs
A delivered read page records the dependencies retained by that page under
{cite}`requirements.sdk.graph.evidence.node_inputs`. Each continuation of a
node or mapped source read retains the original node identity and content
fingerprint; reading a later page does not observe a newer version. A change
to that node's fingerprint can invalidate the evidence even if it happens
between pages. Agent tools record on delivery. Discovery pages record no evidence
inputs, just like their initial result. Preparing an undelivered page records
no read.
